items.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: So one person was in the Air Force, we used to call him Mac, his real name is Harry McCutcheon I think. But Mac we used to call him. He actually invited me to listen to the group.

ctx.x: That was very exciting to me actually. They played in the Ernie Pyle camp. You know after the war was occupation time. Many American organizations they’d say a headquarter for this, and da-da-da-da-dah. They took over a Japanese public building. So this theater belonged to the Japanese, a performing group, a very famous group called Calazipie [sic] — all girls. And they took that theater and made it Ernie Pyle’s Theater. And that’s where they came. And the Japanese are not supposed to be there. It’s off limits to…
Yeah. Something as simple as that, that concept of preparing for your performance.
